1	# Facts: issue #187 (HEAD 7fe8949, Release 0.4.1)
2	
3	The issue and the investigation claim nothing about a browser, platform, crate, protocol or tool outside this tree, so no web search or spike was run (a spike would test only the tree's own code, which the reading below settles). Every open question marked [tree] is answered from the tree; the rest are below.
4	
5	## Settled
6	
7	Root cause (confirms the investigation):
8	- A rerun's plan comes from `review_subject`, which keeps only `Complete` attempts, so failed `review/1` is skipped and `plan/1`'s copy and session are used. `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:10534-10548`; called only from `start_workflow` (`scheduler.rs:7465`; grep of `dispatch/src/*.rs` finds no other caller).
9	- `NO_SUCH_RUN` is the app's reply when `core.run_view` finds no run: `src/app.rs:3915-3918`; the runner turns it into `fail_attempt("review run gone: ..")`: `scheduler.rs:7755-7763`.
10	
11	Q: does any path remove a failed workflow attempt's copy or `artifacts` entry?
12	- No. In `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs`, `ticket.rs` and `restart.rs`, grep for `artifacts.remove`, `artifacts.clear` and `artifacts =` finds nothing; the only `artifacts` writers are the attempt constructors at `scheduler.rs:4453`, `6248` and the `start_workflow` record at `7499-7506`. `forget` hits are `forget_secrets` only (`scheduler.rs:2093`, `2671`). So `review_subject` may rely on a failed attempt's `artifacts["plan"]` entry. Whether the file still exists on disk is not checked by anything; a fix should handle a missing file.
13	
14	Q: what do restart, park and close do with a failed workflow attempt, and do they call `review_subject`/`start_workflow`?
15	- `review_subject` has one caller (`start_workflow`), and `start_workflow` is reached from `workflow_stage` (`scheduler.rs:7401-7412`, fresh attempt or `may_rerun`). `restart.rs:883` treats `AttemptKind::Workflow | GateOnly` as having no restart behaviour (`false`); it does not call either function. Park is the other option of the `rerun` question (`scheduler.rs:7270-7290`) and `rerun_ask` re-asks it (`9335`); neither starts a workflow.
16	
17	Q: serde defaults on `LaneFile`/`PathsView`, and is a new marker additive?
18	- Both are `#[serde(default)]` structs deriving `Default`: `dispatch-control/src/lib.rs:584-586` (`LaneFile`) and `:541-542` (`PathsView`). A new `bool`/`Option` field on either deserializes from an older runner as false/none, which is additive per CLAUDE.md "Extending the contract". Existing fields to reuse: `LaneFile.reviewing`, `LaneFile.round`, `PathsView.plan_reviewed`, `plan_round`, `plan_rounds` (`lib.rs:553-573`, `595-598`). The app's Plan tab consuming them was not read, so "the tab ignores an unknown field" rests on serde's default of ignoring unknown fields on the app side, not on a read of the tab.
19	
20	Q: RECORD_VERSION and migration:
21	- `dispatch/src/store.rs:26` `RECORD_VERSION = 28`; `migrate` at `store.rs:451` steps one version at a time, and earlier steps document "arrives from its serde default" for added fields (`store.rs:455-470`). A new `Attempt` field therefore needs version 29 plus a comment step; a fix that only changes `review_subject` needs neither.
22	
23	Q: `Attempt.revisions` as a signal:
24	- It is pushed by `revise` on the attempt that holds the copy (`scheduler.rs:7620-7625`, per the investigation) and is kept on a failed attempt (investigation l.26). It says the copy was edited by a revise, but it does not say the planner finished writing it (see Unresolved). Comparing files is not needed to know a revision was requested; it is the only way to know the content differs.
25	
26	Q: how do tests fake `NO_SUCH_RUN`?
27	- There is no existing test that drives `poll_workflow` into `review run gone`: grep of `NO_SUCH_RUN`/`run gone` in `dispatch/src` shows only the three production uses (`scheduler.rs:2840`, `7755`, `8445`/`7761`). A test must be built from the fake app reply used by the existing workflow tests (`scheduler.rs` near `12838`, `new_attempt(.., AttemptKind::Workflow, ..)`) answering `Reply::Failed { reason: NO_SUCH_RUN.into() }` to `Body::Workflow`. Which fake harness answers `Body::Workflow` was not read; the planner should read it before naming the test.
28	
29	`show` / paths:
30	- `shown_where` lists only `Complete` or open-workflow attempts (`ticket.rs:1476`, investigation l.20), so after `review/2` starts, `review/1`'s copy is listed nowhere. `lane_plan`/`lane_input` also take only Complete attempts (`scheduler.rs:10843-10858`), and their test at `scheduler.rs:12838-12869` pins that a waiting `finalize` still hands later stages the outline, not the open copy.
31	
32	## Unresolved
33	
34	U1. Can a revised copy be half-written or stale when `no such run` comes back? Tried: read `src/core/workflow.rs` `start_workflow` (l.289-330) and `src/app.rs:3915`; queries to outside sources: none (it is the tree's own behaviour, and the write is by a Claude Code agent in the owner's session, not a documented vendor guarantee). Not settled because the planner's in-place write is an agent action, not code in the tree. Line to build to: if the revised file is complete, a rerun may start from it; if not, the plan must still start from it (it is the newest the owner approved to revise) and must say in the rerun question and in `show` which copy it reviews and that its `revisions` count is non-zero, so the owner can check it.
35	
36	U2. Does `run_view` return None after an app restart (what makes `no such run`)? Tried: `src/core/control.rs:865` and `src/app.rs:3915`; whether `self.workflow(id)` is rebuilt from disk on launch was not read. Line to build to: assume a run can be gone at any time (the `Paused{failed:true}` path fails the attempt identically, investigation l.14); the fix must not depend on the cause.
37	
38	U3. Repro (revise, kill run, rerun, diff). Not run: it needs a live app, a Claude Code planner session and a runner, and the reading of `review_subject` is unambiguous. Line to build to: the plan includes a scheduler test that seeds a failed `review/1` with `revisions` non-empty and asserts which path `start_workflow` sends in `WorkflowStart.plan`; the test, not the live repro, is the gate.
39	
40	## For the owner
41	
42	O1. Did the 09:28 revised copy on the real ticket look complete, and was the runner or the app restarted when `review run gone` appeared (ticket record and runner log)?
43	- Favourable (complete, restart): the plan may start attempt 2 from `review/1/joined/plan.md`.
44	- Unfavourable (partial or the run was pruned for another reason): the plan must still start from the newest attempt's copy and name it in the rerun question and in `show`; it works in both cases.

# Plan: issue #187, a plan review rerun starts from the newest copy

All line numbers are this worktree (HEAD 7fe8949, Release 0.4.1). The
code is the `dispatch` crate; the review stage is a *workflow* stage
(`AttemptKind::Workflow`), not the code review in `dispatch/src/review.rs`.

## Where this departs from the issue

- **"The `revise` note should survive a runner failure the same way an
  answered decision does."** It already does. The note is stored in the
  answered `Decision.state` and in `plan.feedback-N.md` beside the
  failed attempt's copy (`scheduler.rs:7611-7612`, `OWNER_ROUND_HEADING`).
  What is lost is the *revised plan text*: `review_subject`
  (`scheduler.rs:10534`) keeps only `Complete` attempts, so failed
  `review/1` is skipped and `plan/1`'s copy is reviewed
  (`facts.md` Settled, root cause). The plan fixes the choice of source
  and leaves the note where it is.
- **The issue frames the loss as a post-`revise` problem.** The rule is
  wider: a review edits its copy in place under one path from the first
  round (`docs/design.md:2215`), so any failed attempt's copy is newer
  than the plan stage's, with or without a `revise`. The plan applies to
  every failed or cancelled review attempt, not only ones with
  `Attempt.revisions` (`ticket.rs:350`) non-empty.
- **Step 2 of the repro (a runner restart gives `review run gone`).**
  Not borne out or contradicted: it is Unresolved U2 and owner question
  O1. `Paused{failed:true}` (`scheduler.rs:7840`) fails the attempt the
  same way, so the plan does not depend on the cause.
- **"Say which copy it will review" in `show`.** `show` lists only
  `Complete` or open attempts (`Ticket::shown_where`, `ticket.rs:1476`),
  so a failed copy is listed nowhere. The plan records where a rerun
  started from (below) rather than rediscovering it from files.

## The record

One additive field, `Attempt.started_from: Option<(String, u32)>`
(`ticket.rs:266`, `#[serde(default)]`): the `(stage, n)` of the attempt
whose copy this workflow attempt was started from. Set in
`start_workflow` for every workflow attempt; a plan review's first
attempt names the plan stage's attempt, a rerun names the failed
review attempt. Why a field and not a recomputation at display time:
the choice depends on whether a file existed when the attempt started,
and `show` should report what happened, not what the rule would pick
now. Attempts already running keep `None` and `show` says nothing about
them.

Version: `RECORD_VERSION` (`store.rs:26`) at implementation time, plus
one. Add the matching step comment in `migrate` (`store.rs:450`,
after the "27 to 28" step at l.608) in the same style: an attempt
gains `started_from`, absent from its serde default, nothing is
transformed, a build that would drop it must refuse the record. The
version today is 28; take whatever the file says when you start, since a
parallel ticket may have taken 29.

## The signals

None new. No hook event, no wire message: `Body::WorkflowStart.plan`
(`scheduler.rs:7519`) already carries the copy's path, and the app
reviews whatever file it is given. The app is not changed.

## The actions and effects

No new `AppAction`, `Effect`, port or adapter; the change is inside the
runner's `start_workflow` path.

1. **Choose the source** (`scheduler.rs:10534`). Change
   `review_subject(t, subject)` to
   `review_subject(t, stage, ctx, subject, exists)` returning a small
   struct `Subject { path, session, from: (String, u32) }` instead of a
   tuple (it now has three parts, and a tuple of `PathBuf, String, (String, u32)` is hard to read). `exists` is
   `impl Fn(&Path) -> bool` so the function stays testable without a
   disk (a closure parameter: the caller passes `Path::exists`, a test
   passes `|_| true`).
   - **Session**: unchanged. The newest `Complete` attempt that wrote
     `subject`, its `session`, with the same two errors ("nothing wrote
     …", "… was not written by a session"). A review attempt's own
     `session` is the planner/reviewer face (`scheduler.rs:7777-7781`),
     so the clone source must stay the plan stage's session; path and
     session no longer come from one attempt.
   - **Path**: the newest attempt of `(stage, ctx)` with kind `Workflow`,
     state neither `Complete` nor open (`Attempt::is_open`,
     `ticket.rs:858`), *positioned after* that `Complete` writer in
     `t.attempts`, whose `artifacts[subject]` exists. Else the
     `Complete` writer's path. The position test is what stops a failed
     `review/1` from beating a `plan/2` that was written after a
     send-back. `Failed` and `Cancelled` both qualify.
   - **Missing file**: falls back to the plan stage's copy
     (`facts.md` Settled: nothing removes the `artifacts` entry, but
     nothing checks the file either).
   - `start_workflow` (`scheduler.rs:7465`) passes
     `&stage.name, ctx, &subject, Path::exists`, copies from
     `subject.path` as now (l.7474-7477) and sets
     `started_from = Some(subject.from)` on the attempt it pushes
     (l.7499). `new_attempt` (`scheduler.rs:10277`) initialises `None`.
   - Chained failures work: `review/3` starts from `review/2`'s copy,
     which was itself started from `review/1`'s.
2. **Say it in the rerun question.** `rerun_carries`
   (`scheduler.rs:9382`) returns `&'static str` and is empty for a
   workflow attempt. Make it return `String`; its two callers are
   `fail_attempt_with` (l.7266) and `rerun_ask` (l.9373). For a
   `Workflow` attempt whose `artifacts` holds a copy, it computes the
   source with the same `review_subject` call (subject name = the
   attempt's one artifact key, as `plan_rounds` does in `serve.rs`) and
   appends: " A rerun reviews {path}" plus, when that is the failed
   attempt's own copy, " (this attempt's copy, {n} revision(s) by the
   owner; the planner may have been mid-edit)", else " (the plan stage's
   output; this attempt's copy is missing)". The finalize question
   already names its copy the same way (`review_done`,
   `scheduler.rs:7692-7695`). Both the first ask and the re-ask after a
   park go through these two callers, so both carry the text.
3. **The default does not depend on the unresolved facts.** U1 (a
   half-written revised copy when `no such run` arrives) and O1 (what
   caused the loss) are answered by the same behaviour: the rerun
   starts from the newest copy and the question says which one and
   how many revisions it holds, so the owner can open it and answer
   `park` instead. No branch tests the cause. Nothing is built behind
   the default.

## The UI

`show` only; the Plan tab in the app is not changed.

- `dispatch-control/src/lib.rs:586` `LaneFile` gains
  `started_from: Option<PathBuf>`, the source copy's path. The struct
  is `#[serde(default)]` and derives `Default`, so an older runner's
  JSON reads as `None` (`facts.md` Settled; that the Plan tab ignores
  the field rests on serde ignoring unknown fields, which this plan
  assumes and the UI test below confirms for the struct's
  deserialisation, not for the tab's drawing).
- `serve.rs:538` `ticket_paths`: when the shown attempt has
  `started_from == Some((stage, n))` with `stage == a.stage` (a rerun),
  set the field to that attempt's `artifacts` path, found with
  `find_attempt` (`scheduler.rs:9452`). A first attempt leaves it `None`
  so a normal review prints nothing new.
- `main.rs:896` `print_lane_files`: after the existing
